html:
The Ilinden Uprising was a revolt against Ottoman rule launched on 2 August 1903, the feast of Saint Elijah, by the Internal Macedonian Revolutionary Organisation, founded in 1893.

The rebels wanted self rule for Macedonia. In the hill town of Kruševo they set up the short lived Kruševo Republic, which lasted ten days. Ottoman troops crushed the revolt within weeks, burning villages and killing thousands, and tens of thousands fled to Bulgaria. The great powers responded with a reform plan and foreign police officers, which settled nothing. In North Macedonia the uprising is the founding event of the nation and its anniversary is the national day; in Bulgaria it is remembered as a Bulgarian revolt. The Balkan Wars followed.
sum: The Ilinden Uprising was a revolt against Ottoman rule launched on 2 August 1903, the feast of Saint Elijah, by the Internal Macedonian Revolutionary Organisation, founded in 1893.
